faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Dental Crowns
faq.q1: How long does a dental crown last?
faq.a1: With regular daily brushing, flossing, and semi-annual dental cleanings, a high-quality porcelain or zirconia crown typically lasts between 10 and 15 years, and often much longer.
faq.a2: Not at all. We administer local anesthesia to completely numb the area during tooth preparation. Most patients report no discomfort during the visit and only minimal mild sensitivity for 24-48 hours afterwards.
faq.q3: What is the difference between a filling and a crown?
faq.a3: A filling restores a small-to-moderate cavity within the walls of a tooth. When a tooth is compromised by large decay, fractures, or after a root canal, a crown covers the entire visible tooth to prevent the tooth from splitting under bite pressure.
faq.q4: How do I take care of my new dental crown?
faq.a4: Care for your crown just like your natural teeth: brush twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, floss daily around the margin to protect the underlying tooth, and avoid chewing on ice or hard non-food objects.
faq.q5: Can a crown fall off or become loose?

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Tooth Extractions
faq.q1: Will I feel pain during a tooth extraction?
faq.a1: No. With our profound local anesthesia, you will only feel slight pressure, never sharp pain. If you feel any discomfort, we immediately stop and administer more numbing.
faq.q2: How long is the recovery time after an extraction?
faq.a2: Initial recovery takes 2 to 3 days. Most patients return to school or work within 24 to 48 hours following our simple aftercare instructions.
faq.q3: What can I eat after getting a tooth pulled?
faq.a3: Stick to soft, cool foods for the first 48 hours: yogurt, smoothies (eaten with a spoon, never a straw!), applesauce, mashed potatoes, and warm soups.
faq.q4: How can I prevent dry socket?
faq.a4: Do NOT use a straw, do NOT smoke or vape, avoid vigorous spitting, and refrain from strenuous exercise for at least 72 hours to protect the healing blood clot.
faq.q5: Should I replace the extracted tooth?
faq.a5: Yes, unless it is a wisdom tooth. Replacing missing teeth with dental implants or bridges prevents neighboring teeth from shifting and preserves your jawbone.

what.desc: Wisdom teeth are the last set of molars to emerge, typically between ages 17 and 25. benefits.l3: Avoids orthodontic crowding and shifting of previously straightened teeth
benefits.l4: Eliminates recurrent pericoronitis (painful bacterial gum infections around partial teeth)
benefits.l5: Prevents fluid-filled dentigerous cysts and tumors from forming around impacted teeth
benefits.l6: Alleviates persistent pressure headaches and sinus congestion caused by upper molars
benefits.l7: Advanced 3D CBCT imaging ensures exact mapping away from the mandibular nerve
benefits.l8: Smooth, rapid recovery supported by specialized post-operative care

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Wisdom Teeth
faq.q1: When is the ideal age to remove wisdom teeth?
faq.a1: Between ages 16 and 22 is ideal. At this stage, roots are not fully formed and surrounding bone is softer, resulting in easier removal and faster healing.
faq.q2: Can I have all four wisdom teeth removed at once?
faq.a2: Yes! In fact, removing all four during a single appointment is the most common approach because it requires only one recovery period.
faq.q3: How long does it take to recover from wisdom teeth surgery?
faq.a3: Most swelling and tenderness peaks on day 2 or 3 and subsides by day 4 or 5. Most patients return to school or normal routines within 3 to 4 days.

faq.q5: What if my wisdom teeth aren't hurting?
faq.a5: Even painless wisdom teeth can cause silent damage, including bone loss, cyst formation, and hidden cavities between molars. Regular 3D scans determine if removal is warranted.

hero.desc: A severe toothache, lingering temperature sensitivity, or swelling doesn't have to mean losing your tooth. what.title: Saving Damaged Teeth from the Inside Out
what.desc: Root canal therapy (endodontic treatment) treats infection within the pulp chamber of the tooth, where nerves, blood vessels, and connective tissue reside. When deep decay, trauma, or repeated procedures introduce bacteria into the pulp, the nerve becomes inflamed and infected. Dr. Bariki gently removes the diseased tissue, disinfects the microscopic canals, and seals them with biocompatible gutta-percha.

what.title: What Are Dental Implants?
what.desc: Dental implants are the gold standard for replacing missing teeth. They consist of a small titanium implant that is placed into the jawbone, where it functions as an artificial tooth root. Unlike removable dentures, dental implants are fixed in place, providing exceptional stability and helping preserve the health of your jawbone.

what.title: Gentle Soft-Tissue Reshaping
what.desc: A gingivectomy is a dental procedure that carefully removes and reshapes excess or diseased gum tissue. Clinically, it reduces deep pockets caused by periodontal disease that brushing and flossing cannot reach. Cosmetically, it reveals more of your natural tooth enamel, turning a short-toothed gummy smile into a balanced, camera-ready smile.

benefits.title: Healthier Gums and Elevated Smile Confidence
benefits.desc: Soft-tissue contouring delivers clinical and aesthetic improvements:
benefits.l1: Eliminates deep bacterial pockets to prevent chronic gum disease recurrence

benefits.l3: Corrects a 'gummy smile' by exposing naturally proportioned tooth crowns
benefits.l4: Creates an even, symmetrical gumline across front teeth
benefits.l5: Makes daily brushing and interdental flossing significantly easier
benefits.l6: Improves fit and visibility before placing dental crowns or veneers
benefits.l7: Minimally invasive with local numbing and fast soft-tissue healing
benefits.l8: Permanent aesthetic results that immediately elevate your smile

candidate.title: Who Benefits from Gingivectomy Treatment?
candidate.desc: You may be a great candidate for gum reshaping if you have:

candidate.l3: Enlarged gums following orthodontic braces treatment
candidate.l4: Persistent periodontal pockets deeper than 5mm that harbor chronic infection
candidate.l5: Swollen gum overgrowth linked to blood pressure or seizure medications

faq.q2: How long does it take for gums to heal?
faq.a2: Superficial healing occurs within 48 to 72 hours. Your gums will look completely natural and fully settled within 1 to 2 weeks.
faq.q3: Will the excess gum tissue grow back?
faq.a3: In most cases, gingivectomy results are permanent. As long as you maintain good oral hygiene and do not take medications causing gum hyperplasia, the tissue will not regrow.
faq.q4: What foods should I eat after gum contouring?

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Dental Braces
faq.q1: What is the best age to get braces?
faq.a1: The American Association of Orthodontists recommends a first orthodontic screening around age 7. However, braces are highly effective for teens and adults of any age!
faq.q2: How long will I need to wear braces?
faq.a2: Treatment typically ranges from 12 to 24 months, depending on the severity of your crowding or bite imbalance.
faq.a3: Placing the braces is completely painless. You may feel mild soreness or pressure for a few days after adjustments, which is easily managed with over-the-counter pain relievers and orthodontic wax.
faq.q4: Can I still play sports and musical instruments with braces?
faq.a4: Yes! For contact sports, we recommend an orthodontic mouthguard to protect your lips and brackets.
faq.q5: How do I clean my teeth with braces?
faq.a5: Brush after every meal with a soft-bristled toothbrush, use floss threaders or water flossers daily, and avoid sticky or overly crunchy candies.
